headline: Enron may count future gas profits today
text: The Securities and Exchange Commission has accepted Enron's use of mark-to-market accounting for its natural gas trading contracts. Instead of booking profit as gas is delivered over many years, Enron can now count its estimate of a long-term contract's value as income in the quarter the deal is signed.
imageCaption: The Enron Building, 1400 Smith Street, Houston

headline: IBM posts the first annual loss in its history
text: IBM lost 2.8 billion dollars in 1991, its first full-year loss ever, and revenue fell to 64.8 billion dollars from 69 billion, the first decline since 1946. It cut about 29,000 jobs last year and expects 15,000 to 20,000 more to go in 1992. Chairman John Akers blamed the weak world economy, competition and product transitions.
imageCaption: John Akers, IBM's chairman and chief executive

headline: Windows 3.1 ships, and Microsoft wins against Apple
text: On 6 April Microsoft shipped Windows 3.1, with more than a million advance orders worldwide. On 15 April a federal judge ruled that the screen displays Apple complained about in Windows 2.03, and many of those in Windows 3.0, are not protected by Apple's copyrights. Good news twice over, and yet Microsoft shares fell 7% in April while Apple's rose 3%: Microsoft had gained 68% in the twelve months before, so much of the good news was already in the price, and the ruling removes a threat rather than adding a profit. For Apple the case was a side issue; what counts for its shares is how many Macintoshes it sells.

headline: Tokyo hits a new low; the government steps in
text: The Nikkei fell to a new low of 14,338 on 19 August, having lost more than half its value since late 1989. On 28 August the government announced an 85 billion dollar package, including 9 billion dollars to support the stock market and a plan to help banks clear bad loans, estimated at 80 billion dollars or more. Shares rallied. IBJ rose 40% in August.
imageCaption: The trading hall of the Tokyo Stock Exchange

headline: Cisco doubles sales and signs up telephone companies
text: Cisco reported on November 9 that sales in the quarter to late October rose 99% to $126 million and net income 115% to $33 million. It announced partnerships with Alcatel, Olivetti, Bell Atlantic and US West and new router families, including an ISDN router for Japan.
imageCaption: A worker handles a Cisco router on the production line, 1992
imageCredit: Cisco Systems (Center for Cisco Heritage archive, Computer History Museum)

headline: IBM to cut 25,000 more jobs and warns on its dividend
text: On 15 December IBM announced it will shed about 25,000 more employees in 1993, which may mean the first layoffs in its history, and take a charge of about 6 billion dollars. For the first time it said it might cut its dividend. The shares fell to a ten-year low of 56 dollars and dragged the whole market down.
source: https://www.baltimoresun.com/1992/12/16/ibm-drags-dow-down-784-points-in-5th-straight-loss/ (read 2026-10-03); https://www.lmtribune.com/northwest/in-the-red-ibm-to-cut-about-25000-workers-no-details-yet-on-where-jobs-will-be-cut-24f326fa/ (headline and summary via search result, read 2026-10-03)

headline: Nestlé buys Perrier
text: This year Nestlé took over the French mineral water group Perrier, after a contest with the Agnelli family of Italy. Perrier is still recovering from 1990, when benzene found in its bottles forced it to recall about 160 million bottles worldwide. With Vittel already in hand, Nestlé becomes a leader in bottled water.
imageCaption: A bottle of Perrier sparkling water

headline: Intel becomes the world's largest chipmaker
text: Intel has become the biggest seller of semiconductors in the world, seven years after it gave up memory chips to concentrate on microprocessors.
imageCaption: Andy Grove at his desk at Intel
